name: The Cunningham household at 1824 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_cunningham_secor

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1824 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1824 Mr. & Mrs. Secor Cunningham.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1824, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The two live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: S. Cunningham (the family was at Highland Park on the census day). The 1910 census (T624 roll 241, ED 166 and 167) was read for this card's children: the children it lists, and those the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911, are on the card with the years each lived here, whether or not they were at home in 1904. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Elizabeth S. Cunningham

born.note: The 1910 census gives age 21 on 15 April 1910, so born about 1888-1889.

persons.note: The 1910 census lists her at 1824 as daughter, aged 21, with her brother Secor Jr.; their mother had borne two children, both living (ED 166, sheet 8B, lines 58-61). The family is listed here in every edition read from 1898 to 1912, so she very likely grew up in the house and was about fifteen in 1904; that is inferred from her age and the listings.

persons.name: Secor Cunningham jr.

born.note: The 1910 census gives age 18 on 15 April 1910, so born about 1891-1892.

persons.note: The son of the house: the 1910 census lists him at 1824 aged 18, and the Blue Book from the 1910 edition. With the family here from 1898, he was very likely about twelve and at home in 1904; that is inferred from his age and the listings.

persons.name: Hulda Swanson

born.note: The census gives January 1867, age 33 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Laundress" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (laundress); born January 1867, in Sweden, came to the United States in 1890, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.

persons.name: Fred Stump

born.note: The census gives January 1865, age 35 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Coachman" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born January 1865, in Germany, married. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
